MC	<p>fedb_2e5c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3351;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dx, ++, dx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6c31_e2e9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904708;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #904708;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904708;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3853be;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3853be;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3853be;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ch, ++, ch"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a8db_a48b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #81389e;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #81389e;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #81389e;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, nr, ++, nr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>0b26_48de</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #176e4c;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9b3351;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, cp, ++, cp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6af6_59ff</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e3976;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8e3976;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e3976;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, at, ++, at"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3c72_889b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5d00;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6f5d00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5d00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #186785;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #186785;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #186785;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kt, ++, kt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8a34_b343</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904708;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #904708;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904708;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #176e4c;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>1397_83ab</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904708;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #904708;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904708;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6444b8;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6444b8;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>0b39_0fb6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #326d27;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #326d27;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #326d27;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3351;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dn, ++, dn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ad59_8982</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904708;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #904708;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904708;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22619a;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #22619a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22619a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, fp, ++, fp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5d00;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6f5d00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>84dc_4d75</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #81389e;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #81389e;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #81389e;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hn, ++, hn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>eee2_fc5b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #176e4c;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3853be;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3853be;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3853be;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, jr, ++, jr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 5px 8px;">4,000</td></tr></table><h6>Step-by-Step Instructions</h6><ul> <li>Step 1: Find the row for the Parental Type for all three genes.</li> <li>Step 2: Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> <li>Step 4: Determine the map distance between the two genes.</li> <ul><li>D = &half; (TT + 6 NPD) / total = (3 NPD + &half; TT) / total</li></ul></ul><h5>Determine the distance between the two genes MC	<p>1f6c_4372</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596517;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #596517;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596517;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3853be;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3853be;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>b62e_fc35</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596517;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #596517;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596517;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e3976;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8e3976;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e3976;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hj, ++, hj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0b1e_4c15</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22619a;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #22619a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22619a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bj, ++, bj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>768a_d916</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #326d27;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #326d27;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #326d27;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9b3351;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, at, ++, at"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>887f_8134</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22619a;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #22619a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>451c_e0b1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #186785;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #186785;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #186785;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3351;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kr, ++, kr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>21ea_7da5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596517;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #596517;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596517;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9b3351;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>69dc_1792</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #186785;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #186785;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #186785;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9b3351;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>f495_fc8a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #326d27;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #326d27;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #326d27;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3853be;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #3853be;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3853be;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, hx, ++, hx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c681_6f73</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #22619a;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #22619a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #22619a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, am, ++, am"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. Looking at only your two genes, assign PD, NPD, TT.</li> <li>Step 3: Determine if the two genes are linked.</li> <ul><li>PD &gt;&gt; NPD &rarr; linked; PD &approx; NPD &rarr; unlinked</li></ul> MC	<p>7543_baaf</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #186785;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #186785;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #186785;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e3976;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8e3976;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>df09_5b17</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596517;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #596517;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596517;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6444b8;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6444b8;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>04d8_9af1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5d00;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6f5d00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5d00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3853be;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3853be;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3853be;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, kw, ++, kw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>21d7_84d2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5d00;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6f5d00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5d00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6444b8;">Gene J</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6444b8;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>0434_9796</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904708;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #904708;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904708;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #176e4c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>e3c1_e154</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #176e4c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8e3976;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8e3976;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e3976;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, my, ++, my"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3ab3_092e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5d00;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6f5d00;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5d00;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, nw, ++, nw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>37d1_effc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #176e4c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6444b8;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6444b8;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>a30e_cc50</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596517;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #596517;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596517;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #81389e;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #81389e;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #81389e;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, dh, ++, dh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ab8a_9ee4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3853be;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3853be;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>31fa_65d3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3351;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mr, ++, mr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bb39_d1f7</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596517;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #596517;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596517;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #81389e;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #81389e;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #81389e;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, jw, ++, jw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d48f_1144</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03422;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a03422;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03422;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #326d27;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #326d27;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #326d27;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ey, ++, ey"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>86f6_4e4e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904708;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #904708;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904708;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #176e4c;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #176e4c;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bm, ++, bm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a15c_730e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03422;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a03422;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03422;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, bp, ++, bp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>170e_1710</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3351;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>10a2_e600</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #805300;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #805300;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #805300;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>3093_519f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03422;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #a03422;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03422;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #186785;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #186785;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>3ef5_a6c2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #596517;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #596517;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #596517;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3853be;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3853be;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3853be;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, pr, ++, pr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9c20_7da9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904708;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #904708;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>c077_6c53</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904708;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #904708;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904708;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3853be;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3853be;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3853be;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, br, ++, br"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>82bd_04ae</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a03422;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a03422;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a03422;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #326d27;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #326d27;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #326d27;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, rw, ++, rw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7775_2ccd</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #326d27;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #326d27;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #326d27;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3853be;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3853be;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3853be;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, mr, ++, mr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1f9a_2daa</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9b3351;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3351;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, ap, ++, ap"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>875c_aaf3</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Two Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among two genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #904708;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #904708;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #904708;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table class="tetrad-visual" style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Set #</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Tetrad Genotypes</th><th scope="col" align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">Number of<br/>Tetrads</th></tr><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;">1</td><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 4px 8px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" class="ascus" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: ++, em, ++, em"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
